## Contract review — ACCEPT

Head-sha: `dd9303ac18aca10d6db917441390352eabfdab38`

**ACCEPT · default tier, in-seat · 2026-11-07T19:06Z**

This PR touches none of the four contract faces (`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, no `packages/spec/src`, no governed text), so it gets a default-tier review in-seat with no second agent. It is the model #31120 (`ar`) repeated for `fr`, and it carries `Fixes #28107`.

- **Coverage:** 3100 `en` leaves and 3100 `fr` leaves, 0 untranslated (objects 1697, metadata forms 1263, hand-authored 140). All 43 inline maps are filled. Re-extracting with `…,ar,fr` reproduces both generated bundles byte for byte. The file list matches #31120's (`eb68b98149`).
- **Spot-read of `fr.ts`:** the Setup nav reads idiomatically and consistently (`Règles d’attribution`, `Centre d’approbations`, `Politique d’accès`, `Journal d’audit`). It uses typographic apostrophes, and each `nav_settings_*` entry equals its `service-settings` hub title, which the hub-parity test pins.
- **Your questions:**
  1. The 183 recorded echoes are accepted: French cognates (`Description`, `Type`, `Version`), identifiers, lowercase option values and JSON examples. Where a catalog test refuses an echo, the parent-qualified label follows the `es-ES` precedent.
  2. The digest for `nav_settings_access_policy` in `fr.source-hashes.ts` is accepted. The header says a recorded digest is strictly better than legacy trust.
  3. The #28107 test in `plugin-audit` is accepted. That package composes the Home feed sentence, the claim names that test, and its ablation (no platform `fr` bundle) reproduces the card's English labels.
- **Gates:** `dispatch-gates --ran` 64/64 exit 0, 0 NOT MEASURED. `pnpm lint` 0. Docs & code guards 52/53, the remaining one being lane-verdict, which only CI can run. CI on this head is still running.
- The changeset is `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch with `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none`. `plugin-audit` changes only in a test, so it needs no changeset.

**Landing:** at 7535 changed lines the size gate applies, so os-zhuang or hotlong must approve before the queue. The PR is labelled `pm:awaiting-merge` and assigned. Before it is enqueued, the card thread merges main again and reruns `check:app-nav-i18n`, hub parity and `platform-page-i18n-parity` on the merged tree, because `ar` was dequeued once for strings main added after its branch point.

### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, touching **291** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**66** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57675a21470626b71f086d3fba0147a9440a3e03`.

⛔ **19** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 49 pages)`, `snake_case (literal, 52 pages)`
- **33** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **3** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57675a21470626b71f086d3fba0147a9440a3e03` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c97f9713256fdabed47395f19aee4d955fa54061` — the merge of head `e707147883c0a4f5b186eae38b7bba0e21a1a89c` into base `57675a21470626b71f086d3fba0147a9440a3e03`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c97f9713256fdabed47395f19aee4d955fa54061 && git checkout c97f9713256fdabed47395f19aee4d955fa54061
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57675a21470626b71f086d3fba0147a9440a3e03 e707147883c0a4f5b186eae38b7bba0e21a1a89c && git checkout -B drift-repro 57675a21470626b71f086d3fba0147a9440a3e03 && git merge --no-ff e707147883c0a4f5b186eae38b7bba0e21a1a89c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57675a21470626b71f086d3fba0147a9440a3e03
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57675a21470626b71f086d3fba0147a9440a3e03` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.
